analysis:
Examined base text of docs/provider/cli-reference.md lines 1-805. The file_changes map (range_map_complete=true) shows the head adds a date bump at line 3, a subcommand-table row for `addon` (head line 156), a new `darkbloom addon` section at head lines 904-932, and a change at head line 1758. These are documentation only. The new section describes operator debug add-on holds (`status`/`hold`/`release`). It says the commands reach the running provider through an owner-only lifecycle mailbox bound to the live process identity, and that add-ons use a local socket documented in docs/reference/addon-hold-ipc.md and docs/architecture/addon-hold.md. The visible base content is unchanged surrounding text: cache, switch, stop, login/logout, enroll and benchmark. No security control is altered by the visible diff.

The add-on hold mechanism and its local socket IPC are not described in the canonical threat model. TB-003 (provider operator vs process) and TB-010 (privileged helper) are the nearest boundaries. A local add-on socket is potentially new local attack surface: hold placement could affect availability or lifecycle such as drain, idle unload or memory admission. The implementation (AddonCommand.swift, LifecycleMailbox, the addon-hold IPC server) is not in this batch. The head section lines 904-932 are only partially visible because the patch excerpt is truncated. Integration should therefore verify that the socket has owner-only permissions and peer authentication. It should also check that holds cannot block drain/logout credential revocation (A-008, T-053) or bypass memory admission. The threat model likely needs a new entry for the add-on hold IPC boundary.

No concrete regression can be cited from the visible lines, so no finding is raised.
